extra.message: SQL Injection vulnerability in Student.create(). User-supplied 'name' parameter is formatted directly into the SQL query using Python string formatting ('%(name)s' % {'name': name}) on line 43. This allows attackers to inject arbitrary SQL commands. The query is then executed on line 45 without parameterization.

String formatting operator % used to interpolate user input into SQL query. The name parameter from user input is directly embedded into the SQL string via %(name)s placeholder and % formatting operator, creating a SQL injection vulnerability.

Jinja2 autoescaping is explicitly disabled (autoescape=False). This allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks because user input rendered in templates will not be automatically HTML-escaped, allowing injection of malicious scripts.

cwe: CWE-80: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page

extra.message: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Template variable 'course.title' is rendered without escaping on line 14. Since autoescape=False in app.py, this allows injection of malicious JavaScript if the title contains attacker-controlled data.

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Template variable 'course.description' is rendered without escaping on line 15. Since autoescape=False in app.py, this allows injection of malicious JavaScript if the description contains attacker-controlled data.

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Template variable 'review.review_text' is rendered without escaping on line 22. This is stored user input from the review form that gets displayed to all users, allowing persistent XSS attacks.

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Template variables 'course.title' and 'course.description' are rendered without escaping on lines 17-18. Since autoescape=False in app.py, this allows injection of malicious JavaScript.

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Template variable 'error' is rendered without escaping on line 26. Since autoescape=False, error messages containing user input could execute malicious scripts.

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Template variables 'fieldname' and 'errors' are rendered without escaping on lines 16-17. Since autoescape=False, validation errors containing user input could execute malicious scripts.

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. Template variable 'error.__dict__' is rendered without escaping on line 6. Since autoescape=False, error details could contain malicious scripts. Additionally, this exposes internal error information.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: CSRF protection is disabled. The csrf_middleware is commented out on line 27, leaving the application vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery attacks. All state-changing POST endpoints (student creation, course creation, reviews, evaluations) lack CSRF protection.
Session cookie HttpOnly flag is disabled. RedisStorage is initialized with httponly=False on line 20, making session cookies accessible to JavaScript. This allows session hijacking via XSS attacks.

Weak password hashing algorithm used. MD5 is used for password hashing on line 41, which is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collision attacks and rainbow table attacks. Passwords should be hashed using bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: Information disclosure through error messages. The template displays error.__dict__ on line 6, which exposes internal error details including stack traces and potentially sensitive configuration information to end users.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message
